html:
Bahawalpur was a princely state on the south bank of the Sutlej in the Punjab, today in Pakistan, ruled by the Abbasi nawabs of the Daudpotra family. It appears on the 1800 map.

The Daudpotras came from Sindh. Nawab Bahawal Khan founded the city of Bahawalpur in 1748. The state stretched along the river into the Cholistan desert, where the Derawar Fort guarded the caravan routes. It owed loose loyalty to the Afghans of Ahmad Shah Durrani and lived in fear of its powerful neighbour, the Sikh Empire of Ranjit Singh, who took Multan next door in 1818.

In 1833 the nawab signed a treaty with Britain and kept his throne, and Bahawalpur stayed a princely state under British rule. In 1947 it joined Pakistan, and in 1955 it was merged into West Pakistan.
